title: Allocating interleaved burst credits for short-lived sessions via probabilistic attributor
creator: Daniel Kim
description: Background: Several customers reported overcharges for short-lived, high-concurrency workloads where per-request token attribution currently assigns full token cost to the first observed session. Root cause analysis from incidents in Jan–Feb 2026 showed heavy interleaving on edge shards and late-arriving KV cache metrics causing attribution gaps. Goal: Implement a new session credit attributor job that probabilistically attributes tokens in interleaved, sub-second session windows to improve fairness and reduce retroactive credits. The job should be idempotent, replayable, and integrated into the existing usage pipeline with visibility in Console dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end pipeline runs for a full 7-day sample without introducing >1% latency regression on ingestion path
Attributor reduces historical overcharge rate for sampled customers by >= 80% on 3 canonical incident traces
All new logic covered by unit + integration tests; data drift tests included in CI
Canary rollout plan validated: shadow run for 48h, 2% live traffic canary, automated rollback on anomaly
Monitoring: new Grafana panels for attribution delta, late-arrival rate, idempotency replays; alerting thresholds defined
implementation_notes: Design a two-pass attribution flow: lightweight streaming enrichment (prefix/session fingerprint) followed by a bounded-window probabilistic allocator that runs in the daily batch job
Use existing event provenance keys but add session-churn score to identify short-lived sessions; store partial attributions in a compact epoched ledger to allow idempotent replays
Deduping: extend current ingest reservoir with a 24h idempotency token and monotonic offsets pulled from ingestion checkpoints

Performance: keep memory footprint under 2GB per worker by using approximate counters (HyperLogLog) for high-cardinality session sets; fall back to deterministic FIFO when high-confidence session mapping exists
Fallback policy: when late-arrivals exceed threshold or fingerprint collision risk is high, attribute via conservative shared-credit (proportional to request counts) and flag for retroactive review
Secure defaults: customer-visible attribution changes gated behind release flag 'attributor-probabilistic' and logged to audit stream for any billing-impacting writes
decisions: Adopt probabilistic bounded-window allocator vs full causal reconstruction due to 10x cost and 2–3 day processing latency for causal approach
Approximate counters accepted for high-cardinality paths after spike simulations showed <0.5% attribution variance
Use existing ledger storage (billing-ledger-v2) with schema extension instead of new datastore to simplify migrations
comments: 2026-02-20 Daniel Kim: Initial triage — confirmed recurring overcharge pattern for short-lived sessions. Listed candidate approaches: causal reconstruction, probabilistic allocator, heuristic shared-credit. Spike to evaluate memory/CPU trade-offs scheduled.

2026-02-25 Ava Martinez: Spike complete — causal reconstruction requires cross-shard joins and increases job runtime from 45m -> 12h on a 10TB sample. Probabilistic allocator shows promising accuracy with 0.4% variance on synthetic interleaving tests. Recommend probabilistic approach.

2026-03-01 Design review notes (PM + Infra): Add explicit audit log of any retro credit operations and include a customer-facing FAQ draft before any billing-impacting rollout. Action: PM to draft FAQ.
2026-03-03 Eng review: Implemented ledger schema v2 extension in branch, added epoched offsets and idempotency token. Awaiting PR review from @Rhea Gupta.

2026-03-06 Rhea Gupta: Code review done; requested clearer invariants around HLL estimation error and a guardrail test that rejects runs where HLL estimate differs >1% from deterministic sample on controlled dataset.

2026-03-08 QA: Integration tests failed in CI on ingestion rate limit — root cause was the enrichment sidecar causing a slow path. Mitigation: move enrichment into native sampler stage and re-run tests.
2026-03-10 Ava Martinez: Fix merged, canary scheduled to start 2026-03-12 in us-west with shadowing enabled for eu-west. Monitoring panels pre-created; incident playbook updated with rollback steps.
